```{r}
# Show one redrawn figure with its caption and file name.
show <- function(which_key) {
  row <- filter(drawn, .data$key == .env$which_key)
  cat(sprintf(
    "![%s File: `figures/%s.png`.](%s){width=100%%}\n\n",
    row$caption,
    which_key,
    file.path("../../..", row$redrawn)
  ))
}

# Show a figure kept from its script because it needs raw events or has no saved table.
# Restyled copies sit under KEPT_DIR at the summary path; the manifests name the script that redrew each.
RESTYLED <- list.files(KEPT_DIR, pattern = "^manifest_F[0-9]+[.]csv$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  list_rbind()
show_kept <- function(path, caption) {
  restyled <- file.path(KEPT_DIR, path)
  if (!file.exists(restyled)) {
    stop("show_kept: no restyled copy of ", path, " in ", KEPT_DIR, call. = FALSE)
  }
  script <- word(RESTYLED$script[RESTYLED$new_path == restyled][1], 1)
  cat(sprintf(
    "![%s Restyled by `%s`.](%s){width=100%%}\n\n",
    caption,
    basename(script),
    file.path("../../..", restyled)
  ))
}

# Show a figure straight from its run folder (new runs are drawn at Nature spec by their script).
show_run <- function(path, caption) {
  src <- file.path(RUNS_DIR, path)
  if (!file.exists(src)) {
    stop("show_run: no figure at ", src, call. = FALSE)
  }
  cat(sprintf("![%s](%s){width=100%%}\n\n", caption, file.path("../../..", src)))
}
```

Five donors (A3, A6, B11, B2, D1) and 11 unmixing arms. Each figure below is redrawn from a table a run saved; the per-cell figures are kept as their scripts drew them.

## 00 Key figure: one dye's variants

The Alexa Fluor 405 (GLUT1) 1.0.2 variants alone reproduce the full CD8T squeeze (0.382). SBUV510 is a smaller second effect (0.19), and the other dyes stay at 0.12 (`figures/s00_per_dye.png`).

```{r}
#| results: asis
show("s00_per_dye")
```

## 01 % TNF+ and IFNg+ at cut 1

TNF+ follows the spectra set. CD8T TNF+ is 22–32% with the 1.0.2 spectra vs 51–62% with 1.8.8, while IFNg+ agrees across arms (`figures/s01_pct_fixed.png`).

`s188_c102` has a lower TNF–CD8 streak than `as188_joint` in every donor (0.20 vs 0.39), lower SSM (1.48 vs 1.91) and lower tilt (0.080 vs 0.12). Spread is a tie (1200 vs 1270) (`figures/s03_streak.png`, `s03_ssm.png`, `s03_tilt.png`, `s03_spread.png`).


## 05 Why TNF differs between 1.0.2 and 1.8.8

Swapping all 1.0.2 variants into the 1.8.8 setup raises the CD8T TNF squeezed share from 0.12 to 0.38; the 1.0.2 AF set alone gives 0.19. The TNF–IFNg odds ratio cannot tell which arm keeps the real TNF signal (`figures/s05_swap.png`, `s05_count.png`, `s05_af_swap.png`, `s05_coherence_or.png`).

## 10 The BV510 part of the 1.0.2 Alexa Fluor 405 variants

Removing the BV510-like part of the 1.0.2 AF405 variants gives a CD8T squeezed share of 0.11, and adding it to 1.8.8 gives 0.45. Scaling the spread by 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 gives 0.13, 0.14, 0.19 and 0.38 (`figures/s10_interventions.png`, `s10_dose.png`).

```{r}
)
```

## 11 Noise-weighted GLS unmixing (1.8.8)

`gls188_noise` narrows the TNF negatives to about 0.7–0.8 of the `as188_joint` rSD in CD4T and CD8T, and its squeezed share stays at or below `as188_joint` (`figures/s11_gls.png`). The TNF share above arcsinh 1 rises slightly (donor median about 0.65 → 0.69 in CD4T and 0.54 → 0.59 in CD8T). The density plot shows why: GLS removes the small pile-up at 0 that `as188_joint` has, but its TNF-negative peak sits at about 0.5–0.8 arcsinh rather than 0, near the cut at 1 (`2026-11-10_bmv-gls-noise/scores/fig_bv510_density.png`). So part of the narrowing is an upward shift, and the higher TNF+ share may include negatives nudged over the cut. GLS has not been spike-tested, so recovered signal and shifted negatives cannot be told apart yet.

```{r}
#| results: asis
show("s11_gls")
show_run("2026-11-10_bmv-gls-noise/scores/fig_bv510_density.png", "TNF (BV510-A) density per donor in CD4T and CD8T for as188_joint, as102_var, gls188_noise and gls188_noise_spill; dotted line = cut at arcsinh 1. Original style from script 43, not redrawn at Nature spec.")
```

## 14 What the AutoSpectral articles say

The articles site (https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/) documents version 1.8.7; these runs used 1.8.8. A web-fetch subagent fetched the quotes below on 2026-11-10, and nobody checked them by hand.

- **Variants (§05, §10).** “we’re only allowing variation within the range seen in the single-colour control, nothing more.” ([11 Per Cell Optimization](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/11_Per_Cell_Optimization.html)).
- **Dim signal (§10).** “can understate a dimmer collinear fluorophore’s true abundance” (article 11, joint-pipeline tuning).
- **Joint vs legacy (§09).** “So, the covariance approach is now the default option for unmixing when you supply variant information.” (article 11). The 1.6.0 changelog adds that legacy workflows “must be accessed via a `legacy` argument” ([15 Updates](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/15_Updates_And_Issues.html)).
- **speed.** “The options are “fast” = 1, “medium” = 3, and “slow” = 10.” (article 11, “Legacy pipeline notes”).
- **Passes (§12).** n.passes: “Most datasets I have tested show good results with a single pass.” n.af.passes: “is most useful for tissue samples with more heterogeneous autofluorescence; PBMC data typically shows negligible benefit.” (both article 11).
- **Unstained and negatives (§05, §13).** “Prepare a truly unstained sample.” ([10 Single Cell Autofluorescence](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/10_Single_Cell_AutoFluorescence.html)). “Using a universal negative is strongly recommended.” ([02 Control File](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/02_Control_File_example.html)).
- **Landmark gates (§13).** “This method is highly robust for cell samples.” ([08 Controlled Gating](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/08_Advanced_Gating.html)).
- **Checking unmixing (§03).** “features such as hypernegative events or correlations (those skews) are likely to be wrong” ([19 Correcting Unmixing Errors](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/19_Correcting_Unmixing_Errors.html)).
- **GLS (§11).** `estimate.noise.model()` and `unmix.gls()` appear in no article read; [18 Weighted Least Squares](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/18_Weighted_Least_Squares.html) covers Poisson-weighted WLS only.

## 15 Control diagnosis

The 1.0.2 variant code makes the AF405 BV510 spread even from clean controls (median 0.010 vs 0.0018 for zip 1.8.8). CD3 spreads into TNF (SSM 7.55), and Th2 is squeezed more than TNF (`figures/s15_102code_spread.png`, `s15_ssm_zip.png`, `s15_screen.png`).

```{r}
show("s15_origin_shape")
show("s15_offsets")
show("s15_sbuv510")
show("s15_ssm_zip")
show("s15_screen")
show("s15_channel_map")
```

AutoSpectral quotes for this section (same source and caveat as section 14):

- “As of version 1.6.0, we no longer provide autofluorescence information via `af.spectra` when calling `get.spectral.variants()`.” (01 Full Legacy Workflow, "Per-cell Fluorophore Optimization").
- “we’re only allowing variation within the range seen in the single-colour control, nothing more.” (11 Per Cell Optimization).
- “Prepare a truly unstained sample.” (10 Single Cell Autofluorescence).
- “This is now done using k-nearest neighbours, and should be essentially perfect.” (01 Automated Spectral Workflow, "Outputs").
- Beads may not match cells (paraphrase of 05 Preparing Controls, "Recommendations for controls").
- “there is a lot of spillover spread (uncertainty) from BUV661 into APC (but not the other way around).” (19 Correcting Unmixing Errors).

## 16 TNF and Th2 scatter with SpectroFlo as reference

SpectroFlo, 1.8.8 zip and opt188 show no CD8T TNF band at 0 (TNF+ 35.3–71.1%, 28.6–69.4% and 31.3–73.3% across donors); every arm with the 1.0.2 AF405 variants shows one. SBUV510 + AF405 together give the same TNF+ as AF405 alone. SpectroFlo's Th2 rises with GLUT1 along a spillover-like diagonal (29.8–58.0% Th2+), so SpectroFlo is no Th2 reference (`16_scatter_spectroflo/per_dye_TNF_vs_GLUT1.png`, `sbuv510_af405_gap_closed.png`, `th2_Th2_vs_GLUT1.png`). AutoSpectral: “features such as hypernegative events or correlations (those skews) are likely to be wrong” (19 Correcting Unmixing Errors).

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_kept(
  "16_scatter_spectroflo/per_dye_TNF_vs_GLUT1.png",
  "CD8T TNF against GLUT1; rows donors, columns arms (SpectroFlo first, then 1.8.8 zip, opt188 and the 1.0.2 variants swapped in by dye); red line at the arcsinh 1 cut, % above it printed; each arm on its own gates. Kept from script 72_per_dye_scatter_ggcyto.R: needs raw events."
)
show_kept(
  "16_scatter_spectroflo/sbuv510_af405_gap_closed.png",
  "Gap closed by the SBUV510 + AF405 1.0.2 variant arm, CD8T TNF; donors as points. Kept from script 51_score_ablation.R."
)
show_kept(
  "16_scatter_spectroflo/tnf_new_TNF_vs_GLUT1.png",
  "CD8T TNF against GLUT1 for the newer arms (opt188, refined AF, AF405 1.0.2 code on clean controls, 1.0.2 code with 1.8.8 spectra, 1.0.2 zip); red line at the arcsinh 1 cut; each arm on its own gates. Kept from script 72: needs raw events."
)
show_kept(
  "16_scatter_spectroflo/th2_Th2_vs_GLUT1.png",
  "CD8T Th2 (eFluor 450) against GLUT1 (Alexa Fluor 405) per donor and arm; red line at the arcsinh 1 cut; each arm on its own CD8T gate, so SpectroFlo A3 reads 41.3% Th2+ here vs 39.8% in the section 17 flag view, which uses the 1.8.8 zip gate. The strip \"AF405 KO (no BV510)\" is the AF405 knock-out without its BV510 part. Kept from script 72: needs raw events."
)
```

## 17 Marker flags, Th2 proof and the refined and AF-removed AF405 arms

Under the revised flag rule, `as102_var` flags ten CD8T markers, led by CD4 (0.46), TNF (0.43) and Th2 (0.37). The AF405 knock-out without its BV510 part still squeezes Th2 (+0.26) but not TNF. Refined AF moves TNF away from 1.0.2 (gap closed −0.053 and −0.227), and removing AF from the AF405 control changes nothing (median 0.003 and 0.015) (`17_flags_th2_af/flags_screen_CD8T.png`, `flags_th2_proof_CD8T.png`, `afrefine_gap_closed.png`, `afremove_gap_closed.png`). AutoSpectral: “we’re only allowing variation within the range seen in the single-colour control, nothing more.” (11 Per Cell Optimization).

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_kept("17_flags_th2_af/flags_screen_CD8T.png", "Change in CD8T squeezed share vs as188_joint per marker and arm; boxed cells are flagged (donor median ≥0.10, a rise in all 5 donors). Kept from script 86b.")
```

## 18 Spike-in recovery, five setups

With a +1 arcsinh spike, 1.8.8 zip loses most of the spike in 2.1% of CD8T cells for TNF and 13.7% for Th2. Refined AF loses it in 3.8% and 17.7%, opt188 in 4.0% and 22.9% (Th2 median recovery 0.85), and 1.0.2 zip in 14.5% and 48.8%. No setup loses most of an IL-10 spike (at most 0.011% of cells). Per cell, Th2 recovery in CD8T sits left of 1.8.8 zip for opt188 and refined AF (`18_spike_in/fig_spike_TNF.png`, `fig_spike_Th2.png`, `fig_spike_IL10.png`, `fig_spike_recovery_ecdf.png`). ## 19 opt188 downstream and the UMAP neighbourhood test

opt188 raises CD8T TNF+ at the fixed cut by a median 3.6 points and flags only Th2 in CD8T (no CD4T flag). Its SOM clusters agree with 1.8.8 zip at the low end of seed noise (ARI 0.41 vs 0.38–0.57), while MC06 and MC09 grow in every donor. The UMAP kNN overlap puts every arm, the known-bad 1.0.2 zip included, below the seed noise floor, so it cannot rank the arms (`19_downstream_umap/fig_pop_pct.png`, `fig_marker_flags.png`, `fig_ari.png`, `fig_cluster_abundance.png`, `fig_knn_overlap.png`). No AutoSpectral article quoted in section 14 covers embeddings.

## 20 Spike-in recovery, other cytokines and metabolic markers

GLUT1 is the weakest marker of this panel (0.7% / 1.4%), and refined AF makes it slightly worse (2.1% / 2.3%). Only CD4T and CD8T cells were spiked, and opt188 and the 1.0.2 setups were not tested on this panel. Per cell, the refined AF and 1.8.8 zip curves overlap for all nine markers; refined AF sits slightly higher for GLUT1 below a recovery of 1 (cells pooled over donors at ≤0.5: 2.0% vs 0.8% in CD4T, 2.7% vs 1.2% in CD8T; `fig_spike_recovery_ecdf.png`) (`20_spike_in_panel2/fig_spike_GLUT1.png`, `fig_spike_CS.png`, `fig_spike_IFNg.png`, `fig_spike_IL2.png`, `fig_spike_ATP5A.png`, `fig_spike_CPT1A.png`, `fig_spike_ATGL.png`, `fig_spike_G6PD.png`, `fig_spike_CD71.png`). ## 22 Spike-in recovery in live CD3− cells

In live CD3− cells (870–2,903 per donor and level), 1.8.8 zip loses most of a +1 arcsinh spike in 6.8% of cells for TNF (CD8T: 2.1%), 2.5% for Th2, 1.3% for GLUT1 and at most 0.4% for the other nine markers. Refined AF loses most of the GLUT1 spike in 15.3% (9.4–33.7%) and the TNF spike in 10.7%. Per cell, the refined AF curve separates from 1.8.8 zip only for GLUT1 (cells pooled over donors at ≤0.5: 17.4% vs 1.6%) and TNF (11.3% vs 6.6%); the other ten markers overlap (`22_spike_cd3neg/fig_spike_GLUT1.png`, `fig_spike_TNF.png`, `raw/fig_raw_GLUT1_CD3neg.png`, `raw/fig_raw_TNF_CD3neg.png`, `fig_spike_recovery_ecdf.png`). ## 23 TNF + GLUT1 co-spike

With TNF at +1 arcsinh and GLUT1 added at +0, +1 and +2 in the same cells, 1.8.8 zip loses most of the TNF spike in 2.1, 2.3 and 2.5% of CD8T cells, and refined AF in 3.8, 2.8 and 4.0%. The 1.0.2 zip control rises from 14.5 to 21.3 and 43.3%, so the test detects the known failure. Split by natural GLUT1, only 1.0.2 zip loses more TNF at higher GLUT1 (CD8T 11.0% in Q1 to 16.1% in Q4); this is an association, because natural GLUT1 is not randomised (`23_cospike/fig_cospike_tnf_loss.png`, `fig_cospike_raw_CD8T_v2.png`, `fig_cospike_glut1_recovery.png`, `by_glut1_fig_loss_by_glut1.png`). AutoSpectral: the joint pipeline “can understate a dimmer collinear fluorophore’s true abundance” (11 Per Cell Optimization).


## 24 Decision

The user chose 1.8.8 zip (`as188_joint`) on 2026-11-11 (README row 113). Across 12 markers in CD4T, CD8T and live CD3− cells, its spike losses are among the lowest tested, without the overshoot of the 1.0.2 code, and it passes the TNF + GLUT1 co-spike. Its caveats are Th2 in CD8T (13.7%; Th2 is analysed in CD4T), TNF in CD3− cells (6.8%) and CS reading 3–4% high. Refined AF (GLUT1 15.3% in CD3− cells) and opt188 (Th2 22.9% in CD8T; CD38 shift) were rejected (`18_spike_in/fig_spike_Th2.png`, `22_spike_cd3neg/fig_spike_GLUT1.png`, `23_cospike/fig_cospike_tnf_loss.png`).

## 25 Spike recovery vs n.passes / n.af.passes

Raising n.passes, n.af.passes or both to 5 leaves spike loss within about 1 point of the 1/1 setting for every marker and population (descriptive; the final setting stays 1/1, README row "Spike passes"). CD8T Th2 loss is 13.7, 13.8, 14.5 and 13.9% at 1/1, 5/1, 1/5 and 5/5. IL-10 loses no cells at any setting (median recovery 0.993–0.998), and 5 AF passes raise TNF loss slightly (CD8T 2.1% to 2.5–2.7%, CD3− 6.8% to 7.6–7.8%) (`2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/fig_passes_Th2.png`, `fig_passes_IL10.png`, `fig_passes_TNF.png`, `raw/fig_raw_Th2_CD8T.png`). At 5 AF passes, unmixing is not strictly per cell. Spiking some cells moved at most 0.26% of unspiked CD4T and CD8T cells by more than 0.05 arcsinh in any channel, and at most 0.02% by more than 0.5; in CD3− cells the shares were at most 0.08% and 0%. The largest single shift was 0.81 arcsinh (TNF set, CD4T, 5/5), and at 5/1 no unspiked cell moved (table fallback: drift is a count, no figure; `2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/drift_summary.csv`, written by `88h_spike_passes.R drift`; all fluorescence channels, arcsinh units). AutoSpectral: n.passes, “Most datasets I have tested show good results with a single pass”; n.af.passes, “PBMC data typically shows negligible benefit” (11 Per Cell Optimization).

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_run("2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/fig_passes_Th2.png", "Th2 spike +1 arcsinh by n.passes / n.af.passes (1/1 = as188_joint): share of cells losing more than half (left) and median recovery (right), rows CD4T, CD8T and live CD3−; donors as points, median line. Script 88h.")
show_run("2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/raw/fig_raw_Th2_CD8T.png", "Th2 per spiked CD8T cell: unspiked unmix (x) against +1 spiked unmix (y), rows donors, columns pass settings; dashed curve = full recovery, solid diagonal = spike lost; % = share losing more than half. Script 88h (raw mode).")
show_run("2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/fig_passes_IL10.png", "The same as the first panel for IL-10 (BB700). Script 88h.")
show_run("2026-11-11_bmv-spike-passes/fig_passes_TNF.png", "The same as the first panel for TNF (BV510), the control marker. Script 88h.")
```
